# Proxy Design

## Package Role

`proxy` is the reusable pool-scoped network proxy component.
`pool-agent/proxyagent` runs it and uses its certificate preparation output when
launching sandboxes, but the proxy package owns certificates, traffic policy,
HTTP/SOCKS handling, sentinel secret swapping, disk response caching, and audit
persistence.

The component lives in the root module so pool-agent and sandbox-agent share its
configuration and certificate material contracts without depending on server
internals. It has no logger of its own: the datapath, cache, audit writer, and
retention sweep report through OpenTelemetry spans (`proxy.*`).

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    sandbox["Sandbox processes"] -->|"HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / ALL_PROXY"| local["sandbox-local bridge"]
    local -->|"mTLS client cert"| pool["pool proxy (first-byte protocol detect)"]
    pool --> mitm["HTTP/HTTPS MITM (goproxy)"]
    pool --> socks["SOCKS5"]
    mitm --> cache["disk cache"]
    mitm --> audit["async audit writer"]
    mitm --> spool["body / stream spool files"]
    socks --> audit
    audit --> sqlite["gormdb SQLite"]
    mitm -->|"optional"| upstream["upstream proxy"]
```

The pool proxy requires client certificates. Client identity is the verified
mTLS certificate's CommonName (the sandbox ID; the serial when the CN is empty)
and is attached to every HTTP audit row, SOCKS connect row, gateway
decision, destination policy decision, cache event, and upgraded-stream audit
row. The listener sniffs each connection's first byte: `0x05` is served as
SOCKS5, an ASCII capital letter as HTTP, and anything else (SOCKS4 included) is
closed. Every allowed `CONNECT` is MITM'd with a per-host certificate from the
MITM CA; there is no passthrough tunnel.

A request read from a tunnel is for the `CONNECT` authority, while policy —
the filter, the gateways, and the secret swap — judges its `Host`. So a
tunneled request whose `Host` or absolute URL names any other host is answered
`421` and audited as blocked, never sent: otherwise a credential bound to one
host could be sent to another. A tunnel whose client skips TLS is served in
plaintext; if the tunnel is to port 443, its requests still go upstream over
TLS (span attribute `proxy.http.tunnel_upgraded`). Zig's HTTP client
(ziglang/zig#19878) needs this: it sends plaintext HTTP inside an HTTPS
`CONNECT`. A tunnel to any other port stays plaintext end to end.

The sandbox-local bridge accepts localhost traffic from sandbox processes and
splices it, protocol-agnostic, onto an mTLS connection to the pool proxy
carrying the sandbox's client certificate. Its `Dialer` is how anything in a
sandbox reaches a pool service — the bridge, and the credentials relay in
`sandbox-agent/credentials` — and it has two layers:

- **Transport**, chosen by the URL's scheme through [`wire`](../wire), the same
  place every other transport in the system is chosen: `https://host:port`
  dials TCP (a Docker pool's `https://discobox-pool-proxy:17080`),
  `vsock://cid:port` an AF_VSOCK context, and `unix:///path` a socket, so a
  sandbox with no network interface at all can still reach its pool (ADR 0144
  §4). `http` is refused: nothing speaks plaintext to the pool.
- **mTLS**, identical on every transport. The client certificate's common name
  stays the tenant identity, so the proxy is unchanged and learns nothing about
  hypervisors. The pool's certificate is verified against `serverName` from
  `bridge.json`, or the URL's host when that is empty; a `vsock` or `unix` URL
  has no host, so it needs `serverName`, and the pool states it in every bridge
  config it stages.

A connection whose first request is an HTTP proxy request (`CONNECT`, or an
absolute-form `http://` request) for an IP address in one of the sandbox's own
subnets (`nestedbridge.LocalSubnets`, read per request) is connected directly,
as `NO_PROXY`'s subnet entries intend; the pool cannot reach those networks.
`NO_PROXY` alone is not enough: Node's built-in `fetch` (undici), which the

a plain request is sent on with `Connection: close` so the client cannot reuse
it; a client that carries requests for several hosts over one proxy connection
(Go, urllib3) honors the CIDR entries and never sends a local address here.

---
name: proxy-material-grace-dir-mtime-bug
description: "Proxy-material reaper grace window stats only the dir mtime, so re-staged material for old sandboxes is pruned mid-recreate — fails ContainerCreate, OR silently drops the box's sentinel set from the pool proxy (harness 401s)"
metadata:

---

Diagnosed 2026-08-12 (sbx_febbbyq0knzng6yq error state): during a spec-change
container replace, the sandbox briefly has no container. The proxy-material
reaper (`reconcileSandboxMaterial` / `reconcileProxyMaterial` →
`proxyagent.OrphanedSandboxIDs`, run 5s after any container destroy event)
should protect in-flight creates with a 15-min grace window, but
`materialModTime` (pool-agent/proxyagent/proxyagent.go) stats only the material
**directory**, and `EnsureSandboxMaterial` overwrites files in place without
bumping it. So an hours-old sandbox's re-staged material looks stale and is
pruned between EnsureSandboxMaterial/UpsertSandboxSentinels and ContainerCreate.
The doc comment on OrphanedSandboxIDs says "youngest on-disk file", so the code
contradicts its own contract.

Symptom 1 (2026-08-12): `bind source path does not exist` on ContainerCreate.

Symptom 2 (2026-10-21, sbx_2b09q6x14hkmc5kp): create succeeded but
`RemoveSandboxPolicy` had wiped the box's entry from the pool proxy's
`/var/lib/discobox/proxy/projects/<proj>/pools/<pool>/secrets.json` (`clients`
map). The proxy then never swaps the box's sentinel, so Claude gets
"OAuth access token is invalid" 401s while every other box on the same
secret works. Restart does NOT fix it: the start-an-existing-container path
never re-upserts sentinels; only a create (repair/upgrade) or a server
`pushSandboxSentinels` Update does. Diagnose by comparing every pool container
against that file's `clients` keys via `discobox admin pool console`.

Still NOT fixed as of 2026-10-21.

input.content:
## What happens

A discobox can silently drop out of its pool proxy's sentinel set. From then on the proxy never swaps that box's sentinels, so they go upstream as themselves and the harness gets `401`s. For Claude Code that is `authentication_error: OAuth access token is invalid`. Every other box on the same harness config, secret and grant keeps working.

Seen on `sbx_2b09q6x14hkmc5kp` (pool `pool_0hvb5fjmk5dygmt6`, 2026-10-21):

- The box's `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and `/run/discobox/secrets/secrets.json` agree on its `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` sentinel.
- The pool's `/var/lib/discobox/proxy/projects/<proj>/pools/<pool>/secrets.json` has a `clients` entry for every sandbox container in the pool except this one.
- The same request with each box's sentinel got `401` from this box and `200` from another box at the same moment.

None of the obvious recoveries work:

- **Restarting the box.** Starting an existing container never calls `UpsertSandboxSentinels`. Only the create path (`pool-agent/sandboxruntime/runtime.go`, `CreateSandbox`) and `UpdateSandbox` do.
- **Deleting `.credentials.json` and re-running `discobox-harness-run`.** This re-renders the same sentinel, which is correct and still unregistered.
- **Running `/login` in the box.** The real token works until `sandbox-agent/terminal/secretfiles.go` restores the sentinel about 30s later.

Only rebuilding the container (`discobox admin box repair` / `upgrade`) recovers it.

## Cause

This is the orphan reaper's grace check. `proxyagent.OrphanedSandboxIDs` protects in-flight creates with `proxyMaterialGracePeriod` (15m), but `materialModTime` (`pool-agent/proxyagent/proxyagent.go`) stats only the sandbox's material **directory**. `EnsureSandboxMaterial` re-stages by overwriting files in place, which does not bump the directory's mtime. The function's own doc comment says the grace is judged by the "youngest on-disk file".

So when an old sandbox's container is replaced:

1. The old container is removed, which emits a `destroy` event.
2. The create stages material and calls `UpsertSandboxSentinels`.
3. 5s after the event (`proxyMaterialEventDebounce`), `reconcileProxyMaterial` runs. It finds no container yet and a material dir days old, so it treats the box as an orphan and calls `RemoveSandboxPolicy` + `RemoveSandboxMaterial`. That wipes the entry step 2 just wrote.
4. `ContainerCreate` succeeds, and the box runs with no sentinel set.

Here the container was replaced at 18:14Z. The box's material dir on the pool was later recreated at 20:39:20Z (when the box started), so the earlier dir had been pruned. The first `401` came at 20:39:22Z. The 18:14Z Docker events had already rotated out, so step 3 is inferred rather than observed.

Earlier the same race showed up differently: a prune between staging and `ContainerCreate` failed the create with `invalid mount config for type "bind": bind source path does not exist`.

## Fix

1. Judge the grace window by the youngest file in the material tree, as the doc comment says, or have `EnsureSandboxMaterial` bump the directory's mtime when it re-stages.
2. Make the box's sentinel registration level-triggered, so a box that lost it recovers without a rebuild. For example, re-assert `UpsertSandboxSentinels` from the runtime config the pool already holds whenever an existing container starts, or have the control plane re-push on start.

## Diagnosing

From `discobox admin pool console <pool>`, compare every container labelled `discobox.pool_id=<pool>` against the `clients` keys in the pool's proxy `secrets.json`. A running box missing there has this bug.

**Already fixed: the window-title bug.** A note from 2026-08-12 said the terminal parser garbled any title containing `✳` or curly quotes (`“ ”`), which Claude Code's titles use. The title came out as `�`, and the rest of it spilled onto the screen. Every module now swaps in your fork `discobox-ai/charm-x` for that parser. I ran a quick throwaway test with `✳ Claude “x”` and it came through intact. The original library still has the bug, so sending the fix upstream would let you drop the fork. I've marked the note fixed.

**Not product bugs:**
- **Syncthing and `.git`.** On this machine and Station76, git refs can arrive before the objects they point to, which breaks `git status` for minutes at a time. The note blames Station76's Syncthing: it misses changes in most `.git/objects` folders, likely because of its nested shared folders. That's a fix to how the two machines are set up, not to discobox, and nothing says it's been done.
- **Working tips.** The rest are habits rather than defects:
  - Stop `task dev` before rebasing.
  - Use `GOPROXY=direct` when bumping the `x` or `hooks` modules.
  - Force a re-run when a `check-hooks` result is stale.
  - Watch for ADR number collisions on rebase.

The rest are history or design notes, such as the terminal deadlock fixed in July and finished refactors.
